newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Latam soyoil price gap seen narrowing, China buys.
newsitem.headline: Latam soyoil price gap seen narrowing, China buys.

text.p: China is buying Argentine and Brazilian soyoil for nearby shipment, Argentine traders said Tuesday, but they added that South American oil's big price advantage over U.S. oil will narrow.

"China has been buying. Every month they're buying a bit more, but it's not an explosion," said one trader. "There is a rumor this morning that they've got another quota for 100,000 tonnes. They had a quota for 100,000 tonnes a couple of weeks ago, and now it seems they've got another one."
He added :"They're looking for nearby because those are the cheapest positions. I'd say they'll be looking for September or October."
With Argentine October soyoil going for around $535 a tonne, it has an unusually high FOB price advantage of about $30 over U.S. gulf oil.
"If you take shipping costs into account, the difference should only be about $10. The U.S. doesn't exist in this market," another trader said.
But traders added that the price gap will begin to close.

One said that he expected Argentina could export a maximum 500,000 tonnes of sunflower seed oil by March, and 800,000 tonnes of soybean oil. Brazil will only be able to export 450,000 tonnes of soybean oil.
Another trader said that he thought Argentina could manage 700,000 tonnes of soybean oil from October to March, and Brazil about 500,000 tonnes.

"If South America is going to ship around 400,000 tonnes a month of oil, then in less than five months we'll be out of oil, which is not going to happen," a trader said. "What this tells us is that, probably by December, our premiums will have to get a lot closer to U.S. premiums to allow exports from the U.S., otherwise there will not be enough oil for world demand."
Traders said big South American oil stocks were due not to good crops but to more local crushing. But oilseed stocks are low and so the crush rate, especially in Brazil, will have to drop.
"In Argentina we still have enough to crush at full capacity probably for one more month," a trader said.
He also predicted that the big carries between months of around $7 to $8 and will begin to fall.
"First we will start eating stocks. And everyone will buy nearbies, so carries will come in to $2 or $3, $4 at most," he said.
